 Minnesota Timberwolves continues to demonstrate that it has enough resources to compete even without its star player, Anthony Edwards . The Minneapolis franchise achieved a new victory, this time by 106-98 against Portland Trail Blazers , thanks to a spectacular performance by Terrence Shannon Jr. , who recorded the best game of his career in the NBA. 
 The shooting guard finished with 34 points coming off the bench, becoming the standout player on a night when Rudy Gobert also played a key role with 18 points and 15 rebounds. Minnesota improved its record to seven wins and three losses since losing Edwards, who underwent arthroscopy on his right knee on October 29. 
 Shannon's 34 points as a substitute also hold significant statistical meaning. It is the highest scoring by a Timberwolves player coming off the bench in the last ten years, a record he shares with Naz Reid, who achieved the same figure in 2024. 
 Terrence Shannon Jr. seizes his opportunity 
 The depth of the roster has been one of Minnesota's great strengths during the absence of Edwards . Jaden McDaniels explained after the game that the team has different players capable of stepping up depending on the needs of each night. 
 "This shows how versatile our team is. Anyone can win a game for us. TJ did it today. Tomorrow it could be Bones Hyland. The day after, it could be me or Ayo Dosunmu. Whoever it is, when their moment comes, we all want to see them succeed and continue to build their confidence," explained McDaniels. 
 The Timberwolves also managed to overcome a particularly tough night for LaMelo Ball, who finished with just six points after making two of his 13 shots. The player also struggled in the previous game against the Chicago Bulls, where he shot 7 of 25 from the field. 
 Despite this, coach Chris Finch did not express concern about his performance and defended the quality of the shots he was getting. The coach believes that Ball is getting good opportunities and will eventually regain his accuracy. 
 Rudy Gobert responds after disappointing game against Chicago 
 Another player who needed to respond was Rudy Gobert. The French center had just delivered one of his more discreet performances of the season against Chicago, with zero makes in seven attempts and only one point. 
 Finch had challenged the big man to regain his assertiveness near the basket, and Gobert responded with a double-double of 18 points and 15 rebounds against Portland. 
 The player himself acknowledged that he is particularly hard on himself and does not want his poor performances to negatively impact the team. 
 "People are going to be tough on me, but I’m the toughest on myself. I have the highest expectations and standards for myself. Of course, when I have a bad performance that negatively affects my team, I always make sure it doesn't happen too often," explained Gobert. 
 Minnesota continues to win despite absences 
 The victory against Portland confirms the good moment for the Timberwolves, who have won six of their last seven games. All this without Edwards and also without Jaylen Clark, whose absence due to a right hamstring strain will extend for at least two weeks. 
 On the Portland side, Deni Avdija was the top scorer with 27 points, but could not prevent the Trail Blazers from having their three-game winning streak interrupted. Damian Lillard also had a very challenging night, with just nine points and two makes on 15 attempts. 
 Jaden McDaniels highlighted the importance of regaining defensive intensity and respecting tactical plans following the disappointing loss to Chicago, 117-106. 
 Moreover, the schedule offers an immediate new opportunity for both teams. The Timberwolves and Trail Blazers will face each other again this Tuesday in Minneapolis, in the second consecutive game of this particular series. Minnesota will seek to extend its excellent run and continue to demonstrate that it can compete at the highest level even without Anthony Edwards.
